_comment: The single file a fork edits to rebrand every generated SDK. Nothing else in the samples
repository carries a package identity, and no generated file is ever hand edited.
Every value below is passed straight through to the OpenAPI Generator CLI as a flag, which is
what keeps that promise true: rebranding is a change to this file, not a patch over output.
The decision record lives in the platform repository, at
_comment_generatorVersion: Pinned, and the pin is the whole reproducibility story: an unpinned generator turns an
unchanged contract into a changed package. Raising it is a deliberate change with its own
review, because a generator upgrade can rename a method as surely as a contract change can.
_comment_spec: Written by the WinkPG build, on the bot/api-spec branch. The raw servable document is the
generation input (it carries the prose that becomes every doc comment, docstring and JSDoc
block); release.json carries the version and the bump the platform already classified from the
prose-free canonical snapshot; CHANGELOG.md ships inside each package.
_comment_sandbox: The smoke call every package must complete before it is published. The api class name comes
from the operation's OpenAPI tag and the method name from its operationId, which is exactly
why operationId stability is guarded upstream: these three names are generated, not chosen.
Nothing here records a credential. The base URL and api key arrive as repository secrets, and
the smoke scripts persist only the HTTP status code.

_comment_targetFramework: The generator defaults C# output to net10.0, which the SDK pinned in the platform's
global.json cannot build. Verified during the spike: with this pin and the two model name
mappings below, the C# client builds with 0 errors.
_comment_modelNameMappings: DayOfWeek and IPAddress are published schemas whose generated models collide with the
System types the generated client itself uses. Without these two mappings the build fails
with CS0104 on both. Fixed by CLI flag rather than by editing output, which is the bar.
